title: X‑Men Legends Ian McKellen, Hugh Jackman, Rebecca Romijn & Famke Janssen Pay Tribute to Patrick Stewart as “Great Mutant”
body:
The entertainment world is mourning the loss of Sir Patrick Stewart, the 86‑year‑old actor whose iconic turn as Professor Charles Xavier helped define the modern superhero genre. In the days following his passing, a cadre of his former X‑Men co‑stars—including Ian McKellen, Hugh Jackman, Rebecca Romijn and Famke Janssen—gathered to celebrate his life and legacy, describing him as “one of the greats” and a “fellow mutant” whose influence extended far beyond the silver screen.

Stewart first donned the cape of the telepathic leader in 2000’s *X‑Men* for 20th Century Fox, a role that would anchor a franchise spanning two decades and spawning a cultural phenomenon. His portrayal blended gravitas with compassion, offering a nuanced counterpoint to the mutant‑versus‑human conflict that resonated with audiences worldwide. The actor’s performance not only cemented the character’s place in comic‑book lore but also paved the way for a more mature, character‑driven approach to superhero storytelling.

The outpouring of tributes from his former castmates highlighted both personal affection and professional respect. Sir Ian McKellen, who shared the screen with Stewart in *X‑Men: The Last Stand*, recalled their on‑set camaraderie, noting that Stewart’s “quiet strength and wit” set a tone of mutual respect that elevated the entire ensemble. Hugh Jackman, who stepped into the role of Wolverine opposite Stewart’s Xavier, described the late actor as a “mentor” who taught him the importance of humility in the limelight. Actress Rebecca Romijn, who portrayed Mystique, and Famke Janssen, the original Rogue, echoed similar sentiments, emphasizing Stewart’s generosity in sharing his craft and his unwavering commitment to the franchise’s deeper themes of acceptance and diversity.

Beyond the personal anecdotes, industry analysts see Stewart’s death as the closing of a pivotal chapter in superhero cinema. The Professor Xavier character, now poised to reappear in Marvel Studios’ upcoming *Avengers: Doomsday*, will be recast, marking the first time the role moves beyond Stewart’s singular interpretation. While the decision underscores the practicalities of franchise continuity, many fans fear that no actor can fully capture the gravitas Stewart brought to the character. The transition also raises broader questions about how legacy characters are handled when the original performers pass away, a challenge the industry has faced with the likes of Christopher Lee and Sidney Poitier.

Stewart’s influence, however, extends beyond his on‑screen achievements. His openness about his battle with Alzheimer’s disease in his final months sparked a wave of advocacy for dementia awareness, prompting charities and fellow actors to amplify fundraising efforts. The late actor’s willingness to confront his diagnosis publicly has been hailed as a courageous act that humanized a disease often shrouded in stigma, adding another layer to his enduring legacy.

As the X‑Men franchise prepares to evolve under Marvel’s expansive umbrella, the reverberations of Stewart’s contribution will likely shape creative decisions for years to come. Filmmakers have pledged to honor his memory by preserving the core ideals his Xavier embodied—unity, empathy, and the fight against prejudice. In the meantime, fans and colleagues alike continue to share stories, archival footage, and heartfelt messages, ensuring that the professor’s teachings endure long after the final credits roll. The industry now looks ahead, hopeful that the spirit of Sir Patrick Stewart will inspire the next generation of storytellers to champion the same values that made him a beloved mutant and a timeless cinematic icon.
